examples.en: Modern Korean history has passed through an era of upheaval.
My grandmother grew up going through war and upheaval.
I read the story of a generation born in a turbulent period.

examples.ko: 세상이 빠르게 변하는 격동 속에서 길을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm trying to find my way amid the turbulence of a fast-changing world.
Investors are anxious because of the turmoil in the market.

examples.ko: 격동의 시기가 지나고 나라가 다시 안정을 찾았어요.
examples.en: After the period of upheaval passed, the country regained stability.

explain: 사회나 시대가 크게 흔들리며 빠르게 변할 때 써요. '격동의 시대', '격동기'처럼 굳어진 말이 많고, 개인의 가벼운 변화에는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: It is used when a society or era is shaken and changes rapidly. Fixed phrases such as '격동의 시대' and '격동기' are common, and it is rarely used for small personal changes.

examples.en: Citizens gathered in the square and cheered as one.
When fans band together, it becomes a great force.

examples.ko: 위기 때 사람들의 힘을 결집하는 것이 중요해요.
examples.en: In a crisis, it is important to bring people's strength together.
The candidate toured the country to rally his supporters.

examples.ko: 학생들이 한곳에 결집하고 있다는 소식이 들렸어요.
examples.en: I heard news that students are gathering in one place.
Thanks to the residents banding together, the plan was cancelled.

explain: '모이다'와 달리 흩어져 있던 사람이나 힘이 한 가지 목적으로 뭉치는 느낌이에요. '힘을 결집하다', '지지층을 결집하다'처럼 자주 쓰고, 뉴스나 선거 이야기에 많이 나와요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '모이다' (to gather), it carries the feel of scattered people or forces uniting for one purpose. It is common in phrases like '힘을 결집하다' (pool strength) and '지지층을 결집하다' (rally supporters), and shows up a lot in the news and election talk.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 고위급 회담이 내일 열려요.
examples.en: The high-level talks between the two countries will be held tomorrow.
High-ranking officials have just arrived at the event hall.
I heard the high-ups decided this matter themselves.
A high-ranking official visited the site yesterday.
It's a meeting attended by top officials, so security is strict.
The high-level delegation is scheduled to return in the afternoon.

explain: 뉴스에서 '고위급 회담', '고위급 인사'처럼 뒤에 명사를 붙여 가장 많이 들려요. 회사 이야기보다는 정부나 국가 사이의 일에 더 자주 쓰여요. 반대로 실무자 수준은 '실무급'이라고 해요.
explain_en: You hear it most in the news before a noun, as in '고위급 회담' and '고위급 인사'. It is used more for government and international matters than for company talk. The opposite level, working-level staff, is called '실무급'.

examples.ko: 두 나라 사이에 군사적 긴장이 높아졌어요.
examples.en: Military tension rose between the two countries.

examples.ko: 그 섬은 군사적으로 매우 중요한 곳이에요.
examples.en: That island is a very important place militarily.

examples.ko: 군사적인 방법만으로는 문제를 풀 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't solve the problem with military means alone.
We have to solve it in a non-military way.
The internet originally started for military purposes.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 군사적 가치가 높아서 관리가 엄격해요.
examples.en: This area has high military value, so it is strictly managed.

explain: '군사'와 관련된 일이나 성격을 말할 때 쓰고, 뉴스와 설명하는 글에서 많이 나와요. '군사적 긴장', '군사적 목적'처럼 뒤의 명사를 꾸미거나 '군사적으로'로 써요. 반대로 쓰는 말은 '평화적'이에요.
explain_en: It describes things connected to the military and is common in news and explanatory writing. It modifies a noun, as in '군사적 긴장' and '군사적 목적', or becomes '군사적으로'. A natural opposite is '평화적' (peaceful).

examples.ko: 두 나라는 물밑에서 계속 협상하고 있어요.
examples.en: The two countries keep negotiating behind the scenes.

examples.ko: 물밑 접촉 끝에 드디어 합의가 나왔어요.
examples.en: After behind-the-scenes contacts, an agreement was finally reached.
The news spread quickly under the surface.

examples.ko: 물밑 작업 덕분에 일이 순조롭게 풀렸어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the groundwork behind the scenes, things went smoothly.
The diver carefully examined the area under the water.
A reporter was the first to notice the activity beneath the surface.

explain: 뉴스에서는 대부분 '물밑 협상', '물밑 접촉', '물밑 작업'처럼 겉으로 드러나지 않게 진행하는 일을 말해요. 반대 느낌은 '수면 위로 드러나다', '공개적으로'예요. 물속 아래라는 원래 뜻도 있지만 일상 대화에서는 비유로 더 많이 들어요.
explain_en: In the news it is mostly used in phrases like '물밑 협상' (behind-the-scenes talks), '물밑 접촉' and '물밑 작업' for things done out of public view. The opposite feel is '수면 위로 드러나다' (come to the surface) or doing something publicly. It also literally means under the water, but you hear the figurative use more in daily talk.

examples.en: This village's economy is flourishing again.

examples.ko: 전쟁이 끝난 뒤 나라가 빠르게 부흥했어요.
examples.en: After the war ended, the country revived quickly.

examples.ko: 문화가 부흥할 때는 예술가가 많이 나와요.
examples.en: Many artists appear when a culture is flourishing.
People gather in a city that is reviving.

examples.ko: 가게가 부흥하려면 손님을 먼저 생각해야 해요.
examples.en: For the shop to thrive again, you have to think of customers first.
The port that once flourished is quiet now.

explain: 한 번 약해졌던 것이 다시 일어난다는 느낌이 있어요. 처음 크는 것에는 '성장하다', '발전하다'를 써요. 주어는 사람보다 나라, 도시, 산업이 많아요.
explain_en: It implies that something once weakened is rising again. For something growing for the first time, use 성장하다 or 발전하다. The subject is more often a country, city or industry than a person.

p.n: 회생하다 stresses recovering from collapse; 부흥하다 stresses rising to prosperity.

examples.en: On the day the president visits, security is tight.

examples.ko: 공항 주변 경비가 삼엄해서 조금 무서웠어요.
examples.en: Security around the airport was so tight that it felt a little scary.
The exam began in a tense, strictly guarded atmosphere.
Police officers were guarding the street with tight security.
The guard at the entrance of the venue was tight.
The tighter the security, the more nervous people become.

explain: 경비, 경계, 보안, 분위기처럼 지키고 감시하는 상황에 주로 써요. 사람의 성격에는 쓰지 않고, 그럴 땐 '엄하다'를 써요. 보통 '경비가 삼엄하다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It is mainly used for guarding and watching situations such as security, guard posts and atmosphere. It is not used for a person's character; for that, use '엄하다'. It usually appears as '경비가 삼엄하다'.

examples.en: This election campaign was really fierce.

examples.ko: 선거전이 치열했던 만큼 결과에 대한 관심도 높아요.
examples.en: Since the campaign was so intense, interest in the result is also high.
The candidates jumped into the full-scale campaign.

examples.ko: 선거전 중에 서로를 비난하는 일이 많아요.
examples.en: Candidates often attack each other during the campaign.

examples.ko: 긴 선거전을 끝내고 드디어 결과가 발표됐어요.
examples.en: After the long campaign, the results were finally announced.

examples.ko: 두 후보의 선거전은 마지막 날까지 뜨거웠어요.
examples.en: The two candidates' campaign stayed heated until the last day.

explain: '선거'는 투표까지 전체를 말하고, 선거전은 후보들이 표를 얻으려고 경쟁하는 과정을 말해요. 뉴스에서 '선거전에 돌입하다', '치열한 선거전'처럼 많이 써요.
explain_en: '선거' covers the whole election, while 선거전 is the competition in which candidates try to win votes. News often says '선거전에 돌입하다' (enter the campaign) or '치열한 선거전' (a fierce campaign).

examples.en: The CEO declared that he was starting a new business.
I declare that I'll exercise every day starting this year.
He declared that he's aiming for the championship.

examples.ko: 친구들 앞에서 다이어트를 선언하고 나니 부담돼요.
examples.en: After announcing my diet in front of my friends, I feel the pressure.

examples.ko: 대통령이 새 정책을 선언하는 장면을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw the scene of the president announcing a new policy.
It took enough courage to declare independence.

explain: 자기 생각이나 결심을 사람들 앞에서 분명하게 말할 때 써요. '발표하다'는 정해진 내용을 알리는 것이고, 선언하다는 의지와 결심을 크게 밝히는 느낌이에요. 친구끼리 가볍게 '선언한다!'라고도 많이 해요.
explain_en: Use it to state your idea or resolve clearly in front of others. 발표하다 is announcing set information, while 선언하다 stresses declaring your will. Among friends people also say it lightly, like '선언한다!'

examples.en: South Korea and China established diplomatic relations in 1992.

examples.ko: 두 나라가 수교하면 서로 대사관을 열 수 있어요.
examples.en: Once two countries establish diplomatic relations, they can open embassies.

examples.ko: 수교하기 전에는 두 나라 사이에 왕래가 어려웠어요.
examples.en: Before they established relations, travel between the two countries was difficult.

examples.ko: 새로 수교한 나라와 문화 교류 행사를 열어요.
examples.en: We hold a cultural exchange event with the newly connected country.

examples.ko: 그 나라와 수교하자는 의견이 국회에서 나왔어요.
examples.en: An opinion was raised in the National Assembly to establish ties with that country.

examples.ko: 수교할 때 두 나라 대표가 공동 성명을 발표했어요.
examples.en: When they established relations, the representatives of both countries issued a joint statement.

explain: 주어는 나라이고 'A와 B가 수교하다', 'A와 수교하다'처럼 써요. 한국인은 '국교를 맺다'라고도 말해요. '수교 30주년'처럼 명사로 뉴스에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: The subject is a country, used as 'A와 B가 수교하다' or 'A와 수교하다'. Koreans also say '국교를 맺다'. You often see the noun in the news, as in '수교 30주년' (30th anniversary of diplomatic ties).

examples.ko: 무대 위 배우의 애절한 연기에 객석이 숙연해졌어요.
examples.en: The audience went quiet at the actor's heart-wrenching performance on stage.
The atmosphere at the memorial service is truly solemn.

examples.ko: 선생님이 이야기를 마치자 교실에 숙연한 분위기가 흘렀어요.
examples.en: When the teacher finished the story, a solemn mood filled the classroom.
Everyone bowed their heads and observed a silent tribute solemnly.

examples.ko: 뉴스를 보던 가족들이 숙연해서 아무 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: My family watching the news was so hushed that no one said a word.
As soon as you walk into a funeral hall, your mind naturally becomes solemn.

explain: 슬픔이나 존경, 감동 때문에 사람들이 조용해지고 마음이 가라앉은 분위기를 말해요. '숙연해지다', '숙연한 분위기'처럼 많이 쓰고, 규칙이 엄해서 딱딱한 '엄숙하다'와는 느낌이 달라요.
explain_en: It describes a mood where people fall quiet and subdued out of sadness, respect or emotion. It is often used as '숙연해지다' or '숙연한 분위기', and differs from '엄숙하다', which feels stiff because of strict rules or formality.

examples.en: Thousands of people gathered in the square.
Fans are crowded in front of the stadium.

examples.ko: 가수를 보려고 운집한 사람들 때문에 길이 막혔어요.
examples.en: The road was blocked by the crowd gathered to see the singer.

examples.ko: 시청 앞에 시민들이 운집해서 행사를 구경했어요.
examples.en: Citizens crowded in front of City Hall and watched the event.
It's a big match where a huge crowd gathers.

examples.ko: 불꽃놀이를 보러 한강에 사람들이 운집할 거예요.
examples.en: People will crowd to the Han River to watch the fireworks.

explain: '모이다'와 달리 아주 많은 사람이 한곳에 몰릴 때만 써요. 뉴스나 기사에서 자주 나오는 딱딱한 말이라 일상 대화에서는 '모이다', '몰리다'를 더 많이 말해요. 보통 '사람들이 운집하다'처럼 사람이 주어예요.
explain_en: Unlike '모이다', it is used only when a very large crowd packs into one place. It is a stiff word common in news, so in daily talk people more often say '모이다' or '몰리다'. The subject is usually people, as in '사람들이 운집하다'.

examples.ko: 마스크 착용의 일상화로 사람들의 표정을 읽기 어려워졌어요.
examples.en: With mask-wearing becoming routine, it has become hard to read people's expressions.

examples.ko: 스마트폰 결제의 일상화가 현금 사용량을 크게 줄였어요.
examples.en: The routine use of smartphone payments greatly reduced cash use.
The company decided to make working from home a regular practice.
If you make exercise part of your daily routine, your body feels much lighter.
To make English part of my daily life, I speak English even at home.

examples.ko: 이제는 온라인 수업을 일상화한 학교가 많아요.
examples.en: These days, many schools have made online classes a regular thing.

explain: '~을 일상화하다'처럼 목적어를 받아서 사람이나 단체가 일부러 일상으로 만든다는 뜻으로 써요. 저절로 일상이 될 때는 '일상화되다'를 쓰고, 명사형 '일상화'도 뉴스에서 자주 보여요. 말할 때는 '일상이 되다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It takes an object, as in '~을 일상화하다', for people or organizations deliberately making something part of daily life. When something becomes routine on its own, use '일상화되다'; the noun '일상화' also appears often in the news. In speech people also say '일상이 되다'.

examples.ko: 이번 협상은 장기전이 될 것 같아요.
examples.en: This negotiation looks like it will be a long haul.

examples.ko: 회사는 장기전에 대비해서 자금을 모아 뒀어요.
examples.en: The company saved funds to prepare for a long fight.

examples.ko: 시험 준비는 장기전이니까 체력 관리도 중요해요.
examples.en: Exam prep is a long game, so managing stamina matters too.
We should treat it as a long game, not a short one.
The final was decided after a long drawn-out battle.
I started it prepared for a long struggle from the beginning.

explain: 반대말은 '단기전'이에요. 전쟁이나 경기뿐 아니라 시험, 협상, 다이어트처럼 오래 걸릴 일을 비유할 때도 일상에서 자주 써요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '단기전' (a short battle). Beyond wars and games, people often use it figuratively for things that take a long time, like exams, negotiations or diets.

examples.en: When the rain stopped, they resumed the work.
The shop resumes business from tomorrow.
The two countries decided to resume talks.

examples.ko: 운동을 쉬다가 다음 주에 재개할 거예요.
examples.en: I took a break from exercising and will resume next week.

examples.ko: 잠깐 쉬고 나서 회의를 재개하려고 해요.
examples.en: We plan to resume the meeting after a short break.

examples.ko: 수리가 끝나서 운행을 재개한 버스가 많아요.
examples.en: Many buses have resumed service because the repairs are done.

explain: 멈췄던 일을 다시 시작할 때 써요. 영업, 운행, 협상, 공사처럼 공식적인 일에 어울려요. 일상에서 공부나 게임을 다시 할 때는 '다시 시작하다'가 자연스러워요. '영업 재개'처럼 명사로도 써요.
explain_en: Use it when restarting something that had stopped. It suits official things such as business, service, negotiations, and construction. For going back to studying or a game in daily life, 다시 시작하다 is more natural. It also works as a noun, as in '영업 재개' (resumption of business).

examples.ko: 한국어 학습의 저변이 해마다 넓어지고 있어요.
examples.en: The base of Korean learners is widening every year.

examples.ko: 야구 저변을 넓히려고 학교마다 팀을 만들었어요.
examples.en: To broaden the base of baseball, they set up teams at every school.

examples.ko: 저변 확대를 위해 무료 강습을 열어요.
examples.en: They offer free lessons to expand the base of participants.

examples.ko: 사회 저변에 깔린 불안을 무시하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: We shouldn't ignore the anxiety lying underneath society.
The base is solid, but there are no star players.

examples.ko: 그 노래는 사람들의 마음 저변까지 울렸어요.
examples.en: That song resonated deep down in people's hearts.

explain: '저변 확대', '저변이 넓다/좁다'처럼 문화나 스포츠를 즐기는 사람들의 폭을 말할 때 많이 써요. 건물의 바닥이 아니라 퍼져 있는 바탕의 범위를 가리켜요.
explain_en: It is often used in '저변 확대' or '저변이 넓다/좁다' to talk about how wide the base of people enjoying a culture or sport is. It refers to the breadth of the foundation, not the floor of a building.

dis.h: broad base or foundation; formal, written

p.n: 밑 would turn this into a physical bottom, losing the idea of a wide base of participants.

examples.en: The soldiers went to scout the enemy's position.
A drone is surveying the area from the sky.

examples.ko: 먼저 정찰한 뒤에 공격 계획을 세웠어요.
examples.en: They made the attack plan after scouting first.
A reconnaissance plane flew over the mountain.

examples.ko: 우리는 길을 정찰하려고 한 명을 앞에 보냈어요.
examples.en: We sent one person ahead to scout the road.

examples.ko: 정찰할 때는 소리를 내면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not make noise when scouting.

explain: 주로 군대나 경찰에서 적이나 목표 지역의 상황을 몰래 알아낼 때 써요. 일상에서 장소를 미리 보러 갈 때는 '답사하다'나 '미리 가 보다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is mainly used in the military or police for secretly finding out about an enemy or target area. In everyday life, when you go to check a place beforehand, say '답사하다' or '미리 가 보다'.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 1위 탈환을 목표로 열심히 뛰고 있어요.
examples.en: Our team is running hard with the goal of retaking first place.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 챔피언 자리 탈환에 성공했어요.
examples.en: That player succeeded in winning back the champion's spot.

examples.ko: 탈환은 쉽지 않지만 포기하지는 않을 거예요.
examples.en: Winning it back won't be easy, but I won't give up.

examples.ko: 역사 시간에 성을 탈환한 이야기를 배웠어요.
examples.en: In history class, we learned the story of retaking a castle.

examples.ko: 지난 시즌 놓친 우승 탈환이 이번 목표예요.
examples.en: This season's goal is to win back the title we lost last season.

examples.ko: 왕좌 탈환 후 첫 경기에서 팬들이 크게 환호했어요.
examples.en: In the first match after regaining the throne, the fans cheered loudly.

explain: 한 번 빼앗기거나 잃은 1위, 타이틀, 성, 시장 같은 것을 되찾는 일이에요. 스포츠 기사와 뉴스에서 자주 보고, 일상에서는 '되찾다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It means winning back something that was taken or lost, such as first place, a title, a castle or market share. It is common in sports articles and news, while in daily talk people say '되찾다'.

examples.en: The enemy army retreated during the night.
The army retreats toward the mountain.
When it started to rain, the unit began to retreat.
The faces of the retreating soldiers were gloomy.
The staff officers said they must retreat quickly.
After the enemy retreated, the village became quiet.

explain: 퇴각하다는 군대 이야기에 주로 써서 일상에서는 '물러나다'를 더 자주 써요. 회의에서 의견을 접거나 약속에서 빠질 때는 '물러나다'나 '빠지다'를 쓰고 퇴각하다는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: 퇴각하다 is mainly for military stories, so in daily life 물러나다 is used more often. Giving up an opinion in a meeting or dropping out of a plan is 물러나다 or 빠지다, never 퇴각하다.

dis.h: retreat of an army, formal military term

p.n: 후퇴하다 is the general word for retreat; 퇴각하다 is a formal military term.

examples.en: The representatives of the two countries will hold talks tomorrow.
The president held talks with the head of an overseas company.
The reporters waited outside while the talks went on.

examples.ko: 두 회사는 가격 문제로 다시 회담하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The two companies decided to talk again about the price.
The result of the talks will be announced in the afternoon.
We had no time to meet and hold talks.

explain: 나라나 큰 단체의 대표가 공식적으로 만나 이야기할 때 써요. 친구나 동료와 하는 이야기에는 '이야기하다', 회사 일에는 '미팅하다'가 자연스러워요. 보통 '회담을 하다'로 많이 말해요.
explain_en: Used when representatives of countries or large organizations meet officially. For friends or colleagues, '이야기하다' is natural, and '미팅하다' for business. People usually say '회담을 하다'.

examples.en: These days an unsettling rumor is going around the neighborhood.
As the incidents continued, public sentiment became uneasy.
The mood is so uneasy that I'm afraid to go out at night.
Don't believe the ominous stories that have spread around.
The world feels unsettled, so make sure to lock up well.

examples.ko: 회사가 어렵다는 말에 사무실 분위기가 흉흉해요.
examples.en: After hearing the company is in trouble, the mood in the office is tense.

explain: 소문, 민심, 분위기, 세상처럼 사람들이 불안하고 뒤숭숭할 때 써요. 사람의 성격이나 얼굴을 말하는 말이 아니라 주변 분위기를 말해요.
explain_en: It is used for rumors, public sentiment, mood or the world when people feel anxious and unsettled. It describes the surrounding atmosphere, not a person's character or face.
